# Many repositories

## What a folder names

A folder can list repositories that are not under it, in a `repos.txt`
file with one entry per line and `#` starting a comment. An entry is a
path relative to the folder, an absolute path, or the URL the repository
was cloned from. A URL stands for the folder a clone of it would have
created, so the same list can be shared between people who have not all
checked out everything; entries that are not checked out are skipped.

[`clone_url`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repos.html#clone_url)
expands the short form such lists use: `owner/name` becomes a GitHub
HTTPS URL, and anything else is taken to be a URL already.

``` python
folder = mkfolder('alpha')
mkrepo(folder/'nested', 'deep')
(folder/MEMBERS).write_text('alpha  # the note after a repository\n# a whole line\n\nnested/deep\n')
test_eq(_members_file(folder), ['alpha', 'nested/deep'])
test_eq(_members_file(folder/'nowhere'), [])            # no list at all reads as an empty one

test_eq(_member_root('nested/deep', folder), folder/'nested'/'deep')
test_eq(_member_root('https://github.com/o/alpha.git', folder), folder/'alpha')
test_eq(_member_root('https://github.com/o/absent.git', folder), None)   # not checked out here

test_eq(clone_url('answerdotai/fastcore'), 'https://github.com/answerdotai/fastcore.git')
test_eq(clone_url('git@github.com:answerdotai/fastcore.git'), 'git@github.com:answerdotai/fastcore.git')
clone_url('https://github.com/answerdotai/fastcore.git')
```

## The order they come back in

The order is fixed so that a list a person has learnt does not move
under them: the open folder itself, then its direct children by name,
then what its `repos.txt` names, then the folders another workspace
added, with anything hidden dropped at the end. A repository reached
twice is kept once, at its first position.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repos.py#L56"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### discover

``` python
def discover(
    roots, extra:tuple=(), hidden:tuple=()
):
```

*Repository roots for a workspace of folders, in a stable, explainable
order.*

``` python
folder = mkfolder('beta', 'alpha')
mkrepo(folder/'nested', 'deep')                         # two levels down, so not a direct child
test_eq([p.name for p in discover([folder])], ['alpha', 'beta'])
(folder/MEMBERS).write_text('nested/deep\nalpha\n')
test_eq([p.name for p in discover([folder])], ['alpha', 'beta', 'deep'])   # `alpha` is already in

solo = mkfolder()
top = mkrepo(solo, 'top')
test_eq(discover([top]), [top])                         # an open folder that is itself a checkout
test_eq([p.name for p in discover([folder], extra=[top])], ['alpha', 'beta', 'deep', 'top'])
test_eq([p.name for p in discover([folder], hidden=[folder/'beta'])], ['alpha', 'deep'])
test_eq(discover([solo/'gone']), [])                    # a folder that is not there any more
discover([folder, top])
```

## The set a workspace lists

[`RepoSet`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repos.html#reposet) is
the open folders plus a small store file. The store remembers only the
two things discovery cannot work out for itself: repositories a person
added from outside the folders, and discovered ones they hid. The file
is named after a hash of the folder paths, so two windows on the same
folders share one list and a different set of folders gets its own.
`paths` returns the list, and `require` returns one repository from it,
raising
[`GitError`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#giterror)
for a path the workspace does not list.

`add` lists a repository from outside the folders, or un-hides one.
`remove` hides a discovered repository and forgets an added one. Nothing
is ever deleted from disk.

### RepoSet

``` python
def RepoSet(
    roots:list, store:Path=None
)->None:
```

*The repositories a workspace lists, and the operations that mean
something across all of them.*

``` python
folder, away = mkfolder('alpha', 'beta'), mkfolder('solo')
ws = RepoSet([folder], state())
test_eq([p.name for p in ws.paths()], ['alpha', 'beta'])
test_eq(ws.require(folder/'alpha'), folder/'alpha')
test_fail(lambda: ws.require(away/'solo'), contains='not a repository in this workspace')

ws.add(away/'solo')                                     # from outside the open folders
test_eq([p.name for p in ws.paths()], ['alpha', 'beta', 'solo'])
ws.remove(away/'solo')
test_eq([p.name for p in ws.paths()], ['alpha', 'beta'])

ws.remove(folder/'beta')                                # a discovered one is hidden, not deleted
test_eq([p.name for p in ws.paths()], ['alpha'])
test_eq((folder/'beta'/'.git').is_dir(), True)
ws.add(folder/'beta')                                   # ...and adding it back un-hides it
test_eq([p.name for p in ws.paths()], ['alpha', 'beta'])
test_eq(ws._state(), {'hidden': [], 'extra': []})       # nothing discovery can work out itself
test_fail(lambda: ws.add(away), contains='not inside a Git repository')
```

## One row per repository

`overview` is the whole workspace as one table, with one `brief` row per
repository and totals: how many are dirty, ahead, behind, on an
unexpected branch, have commits since their last tag, or could not be
read. `expected_branch` is the branch most repositories are on, unless
you pass `expect`, and `off_branch` marks the rest. Repositories worked
on together tend to drift onto different branches one at a time, and
that is what a person needs to see first.

A repository that cannot be read becomes a row with an `error` rather
than an exception, so one broken checkout does not blank the table.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repos.py#L140"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>


*Every repository as one row, plus what the workspace looks like as a
whole.*

``` python
folder = mkfolder('one', 'three', 'two')
(folder/'two'/'readme.md').write_text('edited\n')
sh(folder/'two', 'checkout', '-q', '-b', 'topic')
view = RepoSet([folder], state()).overview()
test_eq([r['name'] for r in view['repos']], ['one', 'three', 'two'])
test_eq([r['clean'] for r in view['repos']], [True, True, False])
test_eq(view['expected_branch'], 'main')                # what most of them are on
test_eq([r['off_branch'] for r in view['repos']], [False, False, True])
view['summary']
```

## One operation across all of them

`run(op)` runs one operation across every repository, or across the
paths you pass. `fetch`, `pull` and `push` mean the same thing in every
repository. Before running one, it checks each repository and reports in
`skipped` when there is nothing to do, rather than running a command
that would fail. A branch with no upstream is not an error; it is a
branch nobody has published yet, and `pull` and `push` skip it.

`status` runs no Git command and returns one row per repository. It is
there so a caller can use the same code for all four operations.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repos.py#L165"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### RepoSet.run

``` python
def run(
    op, paths:tuple=()
):
```

*One operation across the named repositories, or across all of them.*

``` python
folder = mkfolder('alpha', 'beta')
ws = RepoSet([folder], state())
test_fail(lambda: ws.run('rebase'), contains='unknown workspace operation')
test_eq([r['name'] for r in ws.run('status')], ['alpha', 'beta'])
test_eq([r['skipped'] for r in ws.run('push')], ['unpublished branch'] * 2)
test_eq([r['skipped'] for r in ws.run('pull')], ['no upstream'] * 2)
test_eq([r['output'] for r in ws.run('fetch')], ['up to date'] * 2)

bare = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()); _tmp.append(str(bare))
sh(bare, 'init', '-q', '--bare', 'origin.git')
sh(folder/'alpha', 'remote', 'add', 'origin', str(bare/'origin.git'))
sh(folder/'alpha', 'push', '-q', '-u', 'origin', 'main')
ws.run('pull', [folder/'alpha'])                        # ...and a published one has an upstream to ask about
```

## Cloning into the workspace

A clone has to land in a folder the workspace already watches, or it
would not show up in the list.
[`clone`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#clone) takes a
list of URLs or `owner/name` entries and clones them into the first open
folder, or into `into`. It refuses a folder outside the open folders,
and reports each clone in its own row, so one bad name does not lose the
others.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repos.py#L191"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### RepoSet.clone

``` python
def clone(
    urls, into:NoneType=None
):
```

*Clone repositories into an open folder, in parallel, and say where each
landed.*

``` python
folder, source = mkfolder('alpha'), mkfolder('gamma')
ws = RepoSet([folder], state())
rows = ws.clone([str(source/'gamma')])                   # a local path is a URL git understands
test_eq([r['output'] for r in rows], ['cloned'])
test_eq([p.name for p in ws.paths()], ['alpha', 'gamma'])

test_fail(lambda: ws.clone([]), contains='at least one repository')
test_fail(lambda: ws.clone(['o/r'], into=source), contains='outside the open folders')
test_fail(lambda: RepoSet([], state()).clone(['o/r']), contains='open a folder to clone into')
ws.clone([str(folder/'not-here')])                       # one bad URL is one bad row
```

## The repository a view is about

An editor view that shows one repository needs to know which one.
[`repo_for`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repos.html#repo_for)
tries three answers in order: the repository it was told (`target`),
which must be one the workspace lists; the chosen open folder, when that
folder is itself a checkout; and otherwise the repository containing the
open file (`cwd`).

The middle step is what makes a folder of checkouts work. A folder of
clones is not a repository itself, so answering with it would make every
Git view report “not a repository” while each file open inside it is in
one. Falling through to `cwd` lets the view follow the open file from
repository to repository. Outside any repository,
[`repo_for`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repos.html#repo_for)
returns `cwd` itself.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repos.py#L205"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### repo_for

``` python
def repo_for(
    roots, target:str='', chosen:NoneType=None, cwd:NoneType=None, store:NoneType=None
):
```

*The repository a view is about: one this workspace lists, the chosen
folder’s, or the open file’s.*

``` python
folder, st = mkfolder('alpha', 'beta'), state()
solo = mkfolder(); top = mkrepo(solo, 'top')
test_eq(repo_for([folder], target=folder/'alpha', store=st), folder/'alpha')
test_fail(lambda: repo_for([folder], target=solo, store=st), contains='not a repository in this workspace')

test_eq(repo_for([top], chosen=top), top)               # an open folder that is itself a checkout
test_fail(lambda: repo_for([folder], chosen=folder), contains='open a folder first')
test_eq(repo_for([folder], chosen=folder, cwd=folder/'beta'/'readme.md'), folder/'beta')
repo_for([folder], cwd=solo)                            # outside every repository: the folder itself
```

## Finding one anywhere

[`find_repos`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repos.html#find_repos)
finds repositories anywhere under a folder, for picking one out of a
directory of checkouts that nobody has listed. `query` keeps those whose
name or path contains it, and `limit` caps how many come back, sorted by
name. It uses ripgrep when it is installed, because ripgrep walks a
large tree much faster than Python, and falls back to `os.walk`
otherwise. Both count `depth` the same way: how many folders below
`base` the repository itself may be. Folders such as `node_modules`,
virtual environments and caches are skipped.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repos.py#L216"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>


*Repositories anywhere under `base`, for picking one out of a directory
of checkouts.*

``` python
base = mkfolder('alpha', 'beta')
mkrepo(base/'nested', 'deep')
test_eq([p.name for p in find_repos(base)], ['alpha', 'beta', 'deep'])
test_eq([p.name for p in find_repos(base, 'de')], ['deep'])         # matched on name or path
test_eq([p.name for p in find_repos(base, depth=1)], ['alpha', 'beta'])
test_eq(len(find_repos(base, limit=1)), 1)
test_eq(find_repos(base/'nowhere'), [])
find_repos(base, depth=2)
```
